title: Portable Intelligence Runtime Pieces and Units: From Runtime Intelligence to Relay Localization and Collective Computational Growth
description: Portable Intelligence Runtime Pieces and Units (PIRP/PIRU) develops a structural framework for intelligence that can be bounded, carried, published, received, localized, continued, composed, validated, relayed, and grown across humans, AIs, tools, runtimes, organizations, domains, and generations. PIRP represents discovery-oriented Portable Intelligence whose useful runtime structure may precede complete computational classification, while PIRU represents a more formalized, bounded, typed, and reusable engineering unit. The framework introduces the Pre-Categorical Intelligence Hypothesis and extends Portable Intelligence through Open PIRPs for unresolved intelligence, publishing as intelligence transfer, Relay Context, Knowledge and Relay CallingGraphs, Relay Localization, the PIRP Dispatch Plane, Collective Learning, and Computational Growth. It further proposes that the history of how intelligence is received, transformed, continued, and grown can itself become reusable structural intelligence. The resulting PIRP/PIRU ecology provides an incremental path from today's papers, repositories, issues, questions, experiments, humans, AIs, and tools toward explicit Portable Intelligence and Collective Computational Growth.
notes: Version 1.0.0 establishes the conceptual and structural foundation of PIRP/PIRU. This release intentionally focuses on the research framework rather than prescribing a mandatory runtime implementation, central registry, serialization format, agent framework, or universal PIRP schema. The core release contains eight research documents and seven canonical figures covering Portable Runtime Intelligence, PIRP/PIRU duality, lifecycle and Computational Growth, publishing as intelligence transfer, Open PIRPs, Relay Context and Collective Intelligence CallingGraphs, Relay Localization and the PIRP Dispatch Plane, and the evolutionary roadmap toward a PIRP/PIRU ecology.
